_comment: Albuquerque, NM MSA — Bernalillo, Sandoval, Torrance and Valencia counties. Ingested from the ChatGPT Work research workbook 2026-08-03. NOT YET IMPORTED as of ingest; the owner APPROVED the projected split on 2026-08-03 and it is now recorded in `expected_publish` below, so every subsequent project/publish run re-asserts it.
_envelope_comment: Derived from the MSA COUNTY LIST, not the observed venue bbox (Toledo precedent). Union of the OSM boundary bboxes for Bernalillo (relation/1832180), Sandoval (relation/1344295), Torrance (relation/1832213) and Valencia (relation/1832214), rounded OUTWARD to 0.01 deg. All 24 workbook venues sit in just Bernalillo and Sandoval; Torrance and Valencia are carried anyway because they ARE in the MSA and the rule is county-list-not-observed-bbox. KNOWN SOFT EDGE, recorded rather than tightened: the MSA is L-shaped (Sandoval reaches north-west to 36.22, Torrance reaches east to -105.29) while the envelope is necessarily a RECTANGLE, so the corner it spans contains Santa Fe (35.69,-105.94), which is its own MSA. `states: [NM]` does not fence this one — Santa Fe is also NM. No Santa Fe row exists in this batch, so nothing is admitted today; if one ever is, tighten deliberately and record the row that forced it, as toledo.json did for Cedar Point. This is inherent to a rectangular envelope over a non-rectangular MSA and is the reason the note exists rather than a silent narrowing.
msa: Albuquerque, NM (Bernalillo, Sandoval, Torrance, Valencia counties)
_workbook_comment: This workbook DOES carry an address_source column and 17 of its 24 rows fill it; 7 leave it blank (rio-def-011, ber-pad-019, ber-wes-020, abq-tho-021, abq-ces-022, abq-her-023, abq-dur-024), which came out null and correctly aborted pre-flight. A blank cell here means the researcher did not state where that address came from, which is the SAME fact generations B and C encode by having no column at all — so the same ruling applies and `manual_research` is the weaker TRUE claim, never `official_page`. This default only ever fills a blank: the 17 rows that state their own address_source keep it, because a per-row value always wins.
_geocode_comment: 1 of the 24 venues produces no coordinate from any query rung, INVESTIGATED before the flag was set: rio-def-011 (Defined Pickleball, Rio Rancho) carries no street address at all in the workbook, so it only ever reaches the name-based rungs and Nominatim does not hold that name as a POI — the honest fix is an address, not a retry. The miss is a genuine HTTP 200 with an empty result set, not rate limiting: scripts/lib/geocode-nominatim.mjs throws on any non-200, so an empty result cannot be a masked failure. Set to false so this row imports as a gate-blocked draft in the work queue instead of aborting the metro; the publish gate holds it on 'no coordinate'.
_expected_publish_comment: The projected split as APPROVED BY THE OWNER on 2026-08-05, recorded so --stage=project and --stage=publish both re-assert it and fail the run on any divergence. If a later run disagrees with this block, fix the pipeline or the data — never edit this block to match the output. SUPERSEDES the 2026-08-03 block (count 19), which held four rows on 'coordinate precision low': pat-hurley-park, alamosa-park, lomas-encantadas-park and pro-sports-oasis. ADR-16 publishes those behind the approximate-location label, so all four moved and Albuquerque's entire +4 is the gate change — the re-geocode recovered nothing here, and rio-def-011 still has no coordinate for the reason _geocode_comment gives. Each of the four is pinned to its OWN street (Rincon Rd NW, Bataan Dr SW, Camino Encantadas NE, Four Hills Rd SE), which is a street band on the right road, not a mislocated pin.
